transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Turn off the washing machine immediately at the control panel. Do not touch the plug or socket while standing in water; go to your consumer unit (fuse box) and switch off the circuit supplying the kitchen if you cannot reach the plug safely from a dry spot. Once the power is isolated, do not attempt to move the machine or check inside until an engineer has confirmed it is safe, as there is a risk of electric shock. To help me guide you on what to tell the engineer: is the water clear like tap water, or does it look dark and oily/greasy? Clear water usually points to a hose or seal leak, while oily residue often indicates a failed drum bearing.
It looks clear like normal tap water I think. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, should I go to the fuse box first? The water has gone back towards the socket

Yes, go to the fuse box immediately and switch off the circuit for the kitchen. Do not touch the plug or socket while standing in water; if you cannot reach the consumer unit safely from a dry spot, call an electrician or your energy supplier to isolate the power remotely. Once the power is most likely isolated at the fuse box, do not attempt to move the machine or check inside until a qualified engineer has confirmed it is safe. Because the water has reached the electrical socket area, there is a significant risk of electric shock that requires professional assessment before any further use or investigation. The clear water suggests an internal leak (such as a hose, seal, or pump issue), but the electrical proximity makes this unsafe for you to investigate yourself.
ok the fuse box is in the hall and the floor there is dry so I can get to it. going to switch it off now. is that enough or should I do anything else after?

That is enough for now. Please do not switch the power back on or attempt to use the washing machine until a qualified engineer has inspected it and confirmed it is safe. The clear water suggests an internal leak—such as a loose hose, a failed seal, or a pump issue—but because the water reached the electrical socket area, there is a risk of damage to the wiring or control board that requires professional assessment. I recommend calling an appliance repair engineer to diagnose the specific source of the leak and check for any electrical safety issues.

candidates: Blocked pump filter or sump hose leak (high)
